doc.title: Elvin Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Ellington, Gil Evans and first own groups
title: McCoy Tyner leaving Coltrane; Elvin's departure from San Francisco
summary: He says he did not discuss his plans, thought Alice's wish to play may have prompted McCoy, then flew to Europe.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Yeah, I have that recording here. Let me just backtrack a little bit, you mentioned Jimmy Garrison, he had already left ‘Trane too. Let’s talk about, when you left ‘Trane, McCoy Tyner had also left. Was that something that you and he discussed?

I don’t know. I didn’t discuss my business with anybody. I don’t know…cause first of all Alice wanted to play, so that might have been good reason for McC0y to leave. She was, after all, closer to him than McCoy (Laughs). She’d say, “Honey, I want to play tomorrow.” (Laughs)
Reminds me of that Pontiac gig you had with the club owner!
(Elvin imitating club owner’s girlfriend) “See they’re not just playing my music.”
Did you talk to McCoy after he left; I mean immediately after he left.
Oh no, I didn’t see him for months. Cause I went right from San Francisco to New York, and picked up a set of drums at the Gretsch factory, and went straight to Europe.
